Objednat předplatné Všechno, vůči čemu jsou Britské listy opakem Primárním obsahem současných novin je komercionalizované zpravodajství zpracované tak, aby zaujalo široké publikum, aby je pobavilo, aby bylo efektivní z hlediska nákladů a aby bylo možno prodat pozornost publika zadavatelům reklamy. Výsledkem je, že jsou přehlíženy příběhy, které by mohly pohoršit, a přednost dostávají příběhy, které jsou přijatelné a zábavné pro větší počet čtenářů. Příběhy, jejichž zpracování je nákladné, jsou zlehčovány nebo opomíjeny, nevšímavě jsou přecházeny také ty příběhy, které jsou finančně riskantní. To vše vede k homogenizaci obsahu novin, k referování o bezpečných otázkách a omezení škály názorů a vyjadřovaných myšlenek. R.G. https://telex.hu/english/2026/09/09/krem.text: Menü Kereső Kremlin open to developing ties with Hungary despite expulsion of Russian diplomats English Vida Benjámin Andrea Horváth Kávai (translation) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Russia will provide an appropriate response to Hungary’s expulsion of ten Russian diplomats, Dmitry Peskov, the Russian President’s Spokesman said on Wednesday in Moscow. Speaking in front of journalists, Peskov stated: “As far as this specific decision is concerned, there will, of course, be an appropriate response; these steps will not go unanswered.” Hungary’s unfriendly actions will undoubtedly have a negative impact and are bound to have negative consequences in terms of Russian-Hungarian bilateral relations overall, the Russian state news agency TASS quotes him as saying. “We remain open to further developing our ties. ​We are interested in doing ​so, ⁠and we do not favour causing any harm to what one might ⁠call ​the valuable legacy and ​experience of Russian-Hungarian bilateral relations." It was announced on Tuesday that the Hungarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs had expelled 10 members of the Russian Embassy staff from the country. Foreign Minister Anita Orbán added, however, that this does not mean a severing of diplomatic ties with Russia and said that Hungary intends to continue the necessary dialogue based on mutual respect and in compliance with the rules. András Rácz, Deputy Director General of the Hungarian Institute of International Affairs, told Telex that based on the rules of diplomatic language, one can infer from the Foreign Minister's statement that the ten Russian diplomats expelled from Hungary were in fact working under diplomatic cover and engaging in intelligence activities. The announcement could be a message to Russia that a new era is coming and that Hungary will no longer go easy on Russian intelligence agents. However, it is also possible that this message is not intended for Moscow, but rather for Hungary’s Western allies and partners who have not been able to trust the Hungarians for quite some time due to the previous administration's close relationship with Russia. The spokesperson for the Russian Foreign Ministry initially reacted to the news by promising a “harsh and painful” response. “First of all, we will do the same. But Hungary’s decision could also lead to a decrease in the number of joint economic projects with Russia,” Alexey Chepa, vice chairman of the State Duma’s Committee on International Affairs told the Russian news agency TASS. Photograph: Katherine Hensel/National Park Service/AP Arizona Human remains found in Arizona after deadly Grand Canyon flash floods Hiker Timothy Smith, 53, missing after late-August floods but officials decline to identify remains Uwa Ede-Osifo Tue 15 Sep 2026 21.43 EDT Last modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 21.44 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Human remains have been discovered near Arizona’s Crystal Rapids, over two weeks after a flash flood tore through the Grand Canyon, leaving two people dead and one person missing. National Park Service personnel recovered the remains, before transferring them to the Coconino county medical examiner’s office, the agency confirmed over email. In late August, heavy rains brought a deluge of flood water barreling through the Grand Canyon national park. The bodies of a Texas chiropractor and a martial artist were recovered, according to the Associated Press. One hiker, Timothy Smith, a 53-year-old pilot from Wyoming, is unaccounted for. The National Park Service did not identify who the remains belonged to, adding that no further information would be available at this time. A Facebook account appearing to belong to the wife of the missing pilot, Carrie Smith, acknowledged the discovery of human remains. “We ask that you continue to pray alongside us! Please be considerate of those handling the situation and those going through this difficult time,” Smith wrote in a Tuesday post. In earlier Facebook posts, Smith described her husband as an outdoors aficionado. “Tim loves to show us somewhere new and take us back to the places we love,” she wrote. “We know the search teams are working hard to bring Tim home to us.” Explore more on these topics Arizona news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/27/iran.text: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy claims to have intercepted a US underwater vehicle during a reconnaissance mission in the Strait of Hormuz, but the US military denied the Iranian claim shortly after.In a statement, the IRGC Navy said it had seized the vessel following a "coordinated intelligence and electronic warfare operation". They further claim that the vehicle is a REMUS 600 and has been handed over to Iranian military experts "to retrieve its data".According to Iranian media, REMUS 600 autonomous underwater vehicles are used by the US Navy and several NATO member states. They are relatively lightweight, modular systems compared with larger ocean-going submersibles.Equipped with various sensors, cameras and advanced sonar systems, the vehicles are primarily designed for surveillance, seabed mapping, mine countermeasures and underwater inspections and can operate at depths of up to 600 metres.The US CENTCOM, which coordinates US military operations in the Middle East, denied the Iranian claims shortly after. In a statement to Al Jazeera, CENTCOM spokesman Captain Tim Hawkins said the US has “positive control of all of our operational drone assets."It is the second time in recent days that Tehran has claimed to have seized US underwater equipment.On Tuesday, the IRGC announced that it had intercepted another autonomous underwater vehicle, identified as a Dive-LD manufactured by US defence company Anduril, near the entrance to the strategically important Strait of Hormuz. Washington has yet to publicly respond to that claim.IRGC claims Strait of Hormuz is still closedIn the final part of its statement, the IRGC Navy reiterated Tehran's claim that "the Strait of Hormuz is closed", warning that its forces would confront any unauthorised passage or military activity in the waterway.Also on Sunday, the commander in chief of Iran's army, Major General Amir Hatami, reaffirmed Iran's control and sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz, saying that the waterway “is the strait of our honour, and we will not allow the enemies of the country to use this great logistical bottleneck.”He also called on the Gulf countries once again to push US forces out of the region claiming that "security in the region will not happen except with the removal of the United States and the Zionist regime – and this is not far away.”Hatami also said “the war is not over; we have won, but we must consolidate this victory, and the aggressor enemy, which has suffered severe blows, must still be ready to receive severe blows from the dear Iranian soldiers."But US President Donald Trump told the US media on Sunday that oil prices will decrease “as soon as Iran gives up, as soon as the war is over, which will be soon”.

https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/ukraine-w.text: Guardian staff and agencies Updated Wed, September 23, 2026 at 3:19 AM UTC 0 Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US president Donald Trump shake hands during a meeting in New York, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).Photograph: Ukrainian Presidential Press Service Handout/EPA Volodymyr Zelenskyy discussed with Donald Trump on Tuesday efforts to end the 4-year-old war with Russia , ⁠including a potential bilateral ceasefire ​on energy-related targets. “We are ready for any kind of format of energy ceasefire” if Russia agrees to “not attack our energy system,” Zelenskyy told journalists after meeting with Trump at the UN headquarters in New York. The Ukrainian leader expressed hope the “American side will find a way … to bring them to any kind of negotiations.” Zelenskyy said that he also was ready to meet the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, ​at a trilateral meeting with Trump. Trump insisted he was working with both sides to end the war, despite little evidence of Putin being open to any settlement . “It’s going to happen, I think, more quickly than people understand,” Trump said in his UN speech. Efforts led by Washington to broker a deal to end the hostilities, which have raged since Russia launched its all-out invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, have stalled in recent months as the US has shifted focus to its war against Iran. Zelenskyy claimed the war with Russia would end if Trump applied more pressure on Putin, and if China and India stop buying oil from Russia . “It’s enough to stop them, they will not have enough money,” Zelenskyy told The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday. Zelenskyy said Russia’s energy sales to China, India and Turkey were propping up Russia’s economy. During the same interview, Zelenskyy said that Trump on Tuesday did not ask him to stop bombing Russian oil refineries. However, he acknowledged the issue has been raised before by American partners over concerns of rising energy prices. Zelenskyy also met with the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, in New York, who said he lobbied Trump ​to press for a Ukraine-Russia energy ceasefire in his meeting with his Ukrainian counterpart. Burnham promised further financial support to Kyiv for infrastructure. Putin is becoming “increasingly cavalier, dangerous and risk accepting,” as his war in Ukraine drags on and as he seeks to divide western allies , Nato’s deputy commander in Europe said Tuesday. Air Chief Marshal Sir John Stringer spoke to The Associated Press at a security conference in Estonia amid warnings from some European leaders that Moscow is planning to test Nato’s collective defence pact with bolder attacks that have already included sabotage and espionage. Stringer warned that Nato members need to be aware of the “febrile environment” and be careful in their response because Putin would like to provoke the alliance into an “overreaction”. Officials in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, which border Russia, have been more cautious about the prospect of a serious escalation . “Ukraine is fighting. Russia is absorbed in Ukraine. We do not observe any buildup near our borders. And from that part, I think that most would agree that the perspective of direct military attack is not correct,” Latvian president Edgars Rinkevics told reporters on the sidelines of the UN meeting. European countries have already faced multiple incursions of Russian drones – and several missiles – as well as a campaign of covert Russian disruption which began after the war. Ukraine has continued to press the US for more Patriot interceptors to defend against Russia’s ballistic missiles, but is yet to get any confirmation , Zelenskyy told reporters. “They are positive to help us, but I didn’t get the very concrete answer,” he said. Defence experts say the US has been experiencing a global shortage of Patriot interceptors because many have been expended to defend against Iranian attacks on US and allied bases in Middle East. Zelenskyy spoke of the urgency of needing the weapons, which can shoot down Russia’s more advanced ballistic missiles. The shortage in Ukraine has left Kyiv and other cities increasingly exposed to devastating attacks.
